title: Directional scopaesthesia paper from almost a thousand case histories

tellings.quote: my most recent paper on the subject is called directional scalesia and its implications for theories of and by examining almost a thousand case histories of people responding to being looked at

plain: The biologist Rupert Sheldrake says he studied almost a thousand accounts of people who sensed they were being looked at and turned toward whoever was staring. He wrote this up in his most recent paper on the subject, "Directional Scopaesthesia and its Implications for Theories of Vision" (scopaesthesia is the feeling of being stared at). As Sheldrake tells it, the cases point to a different idea of how vision works, one where looking might reach out beyond the eyes.
